facts.text: On this date in 1962, Kennedy announced the Cuban Missile Crisis to the American public — 13 days after U.S. spy planes had already spotted the Soviet missiles.
On this date in 1844, the Bahá'í calendar began. It remains the world's newest major religious calendar, still used by ~8 million people across 190 countries.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire United States — within a 1,000 km radius, the population exceeds 330 million.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface lake water.
The city of Istanbul spans two continents, but less than 3% of its population lives on the Asian side — the European shore holds a metropolis of over 12 million.

On this date in 1987, global markets were still reeling from Black Monday — the Dow had just shed 22.6% in a single session two days prior, the largest one-day percentage drop in its history, dwarfing even the 1929 crash.
On October 22, 1986, Reagan signed the Tax Reform Act, collapsing 15 tax brackets into 2 and cutting the top rate from 50% to 28% — the lowest it had been since 1931.
The Dutch East India Company, history's first publicly traded corporation, was so dominant it once accounted for roughly 1.5% of global GDP — a scale no single company has come close to since.

Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway holds more cash than the GDP of most countries. Its 2024 cash pile briefly exceeded $325 billion, surpassing the entire market cap of all but a handful of S&P 500 companies.

The U.S. penny costs about 3.7 cents to produce. The government has lost money on every penny minted for nearly two decades, yet Congress keeps the coin alive largely due to lobbying from zinc producers.

On this date in 1938, the first xerographic image was made — a technology based on the quantum tunneling of electrons across selenium, a phenomenon its inventor Chester Carlson borrowed entirely from physics, not engineering.
On October 22, 1966, the Soviet Luna 12 began orbiting the Moon. Its data confirmed the lunar surface could support a lander — scientists had genuinely feared spacecraft might sink into deep dust.

Your skeleton is not static. Every decade, you replace roughly 10% of your bone mass through a process called remodeling, meaning the femur you were born with no longer contains a single original atom.

A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth — not metaphorically, but by direct calculation from measured densities.

Mantis shrimp see with 16 types of photoreceptors compared to humans' 3, yet they process color worse than we do. More channels, paradoxically, means the brain offloads comparison — seeing becomes a reflex, not a thought.
On this day in 1962, Kennedy announced the Cuban Missile Crisis to the world. The speech lasted 18 minutes. The world had roughly 13 days to exist, or not.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Lectures began around 1096; Tenochtitlán wasn't founded until 1325.
On this day in 1797, André-Jacques Garnerin made the first parachute jump, from 3,200 feet over Paris. He had no way to test whether it would work beforehand.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was born 2,500 years after it was built, died 2,000 years before Apollo 11.
Nintendo was founded in 1889, when it made playing cards. The company was 85 years old before it released its first video game console.

Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already behaves like a word that has always existed.
Mamihlapinatapai: a Yaghan word meaning a look shared between two people who both want something but won't initiate it. Linguists once called Yaghan the world's most succinct untranslatable word.
On this day in 1797, André-Jacques Garnerin made the first recorded parachute jump over Paris. The French word parachute comes from para (to shield) and chute (fall) — a verb dressed up as a noun.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a longing for a home that may never have existed, carrying grief, nostalgia, and yearning simultaneously. English has no single word for it, which is itself a kind of hiraeth.

Petrichor — that smell of rain on dry earth — was only named in 1964, by Australian scientists Isabel Joy Bear and Richard Thomas. From Greek petra (stone) and ichor, the fluid said to run in the veins of the gods.
On Oct 22, 2013, the FBI auctioned the first batch of Silk Road Bitcoin—144,336 BTC seized from Ross Ulbricht. The U.S. government became one of the largest single Bitcoin holders overnight.
On Oct 22, 2020, PayPal announced native crypto buying for its 346 million users, triggering Bitcoin's break above $13,000 for the first time since 2019.

Ethereum's consensus layer runs on a separate peer-to-peer network from its execution layer. The two chains merged at TTD 58750000000000000000000 in September 2022, a single integer that ended proof-of-work.

Bitcoin's timelock opcode OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY sat unused in the codebase for years before BIP 65 activated it in 2015—its predecessor, OP_NOP2, was intentionally a no-op to preserve backward compatibility.

The largest single Ethereum transaction by fee was paid in September 2020: a Korean exchange accidentally sent 10,668 ETH (~$5.2M) as gas for a $130 transfer, a keying error that fee-sharing miners quietly split.

On this date in 2015, Google announced it had been running neural networks in production since 2012—meaning Gmail's spam filter had quietly become one of the world's largest deep learning deployments before anyone used the term commercially.
On this date in 2022, Meta released the full weights of OPT-175B publicly, the first time a model matching GPT-3's scale was handed to researchers without a waitlist or API gate.

AlphaFold2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins—essentially the entire known proteome—in a project that would have taken conventional methods longer than the age of the universe to complete.

The transformer architecture, now the backbone of nearly every frontier AI system, was introduced in a 2017 paper by eight Google authors. Six of them left to found or co-found competing AI companies.

GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity—comparable to the annual consumption of about 4,600 average US households, for a single model training pass.
